🪵🔨 A Little Father-and-Son Project That Might Turn Into Something More!

Waylon and I recently worked on these two flower boxes that we’re donating to the Cub Scouts. They’ll be painting and finishing them before putting them in the park to replace the older flower boxes.

One thing I’ve noticed lately is that Waylon has developed a pretty serious interest in woodworking, and it’s something I’d really like to encourage.

So I’ve been tossing around the idea of taking a few preorders and turning this into something we can work on together.

It’s not just about making a little extra money. I want him to learn how to build things with his own hands, take pride in his work, understand what materials cost, and see what goes into earning a dollar. And if it means spending more time together in the shop, that’s even better.

We’re thinking about offering these handmade farmhouse flower boxes starting at $80 for standard white pine, with options for exterior finishes, pressure-treated pine, and cedar. Larger boxes could also be made to order with custom pricing.

🎄 We’d like to offer a few preorders for Christmas gifts and another round before spring planting season.

We’re not looking to start some huge woodworking business. Just something we can enjoy doing together while giving Waylon an opportunity to learn something new.

Before we start buying more lumber, though, we’d like to see if there’s actually any interest.

Would anyone be interested in ordering one of these?

Feel free to comment or message us! 🌱

A little kindness made a big difference today. 💚

I was at the post office with a dead battery and jumper cables hanging out from under the hood when Jesse and his family stopped and offered to give me a jump.

They took time out of their day to help someone who needed it, and we’re incredibly thankful.

At Roswell Family Farm, looking out for our neighbors means a lot to us. Jesse and his family showed that same care for their community today, and we wanted to return the kindness.

We’re putting together an early Thanksgiving package for their family as a thank-you from ours. It’s a small way to show how much we appreciate them stopping to help.

Jesse, thank you to you and your family. You made a frustrating day a whole lot better. 🦃💚

— AJ & Emily
Roswell Family Farm
